title: Mixed serve observed after routing fingerprint collision during canary rollout
creator: Liam Chen
description: During a routine canary promotion for model-version v2026-03-b, we observed a transient mixed-serve state where a subset of requests were routed to an older pinned variant while the canary was partially promoted. This caused inconsistent responses for customers and elevated error rates for 12 minutes. This ticket captures the investigation, root cause analysis, mitigations, and actionable follow-ups.
incident_summary: At 2026-03-01T10:12:00Z a canary promotion initiated a staged traffic shift. At 10:15:37Z we began seeing a split where ~8% of traffic targeted a previously pinned variant that should have been fully demoted. The condition lasted until the manual rollback and reapplication of routing rules at 10:27:00Z. Error rates (5xx) for the affected tenant cohort increased from baseline 0.3% to 3.8% and latency p95 rose by ~120ms.
timeline: 2026-03-01T10:14:50Z - First anomalous route mismatch alert from staging-proxy (route-hash drift)
2026-03-01T10:15:37Z - Synthetic tests detect inconsistent model outputs across identical inputs
2026-03-01T10:16:05Z - Ops paged; mitigation plan invoked (traffic freeze + audit)
2026-03-01T10:21:42Z - Investigation: observed identical routing fingerprints mapping to two distinct route objects due to hash collision in route-predicate serializer
2026-03-01T10:25:00Z - Attempted automated rollback failed due to pin-check preventing demotion (version pin invariants)
2026-03-01T10:27:00Z - Manual rollback and pin reconciliation completed; mixed serve resolved by 10:28:30Z
2026-03-01T11:00:00Z - Post-incident monitoring window opened; no recurrence observed
root_cause: A non-deterministic hash collision in the route-predicate serializer caused two different route configurations (canary and legacy pin) to produce the same routing fingerprint. The router uses fingerprints as a fast index; collisions allowed both route objects to be considered identical during a short window while metadata fanout lagged. A safety check designed to prevent demoting pinned versions (pin invariant) blocked the automated rollback, prolonging mixed-serve until manual reconciliation.
mitigations_performed: Immediate traffic freeze on canary promotion
Manual reconciliation of version pins and explicit re-application of canonical route IDs
Expanded monitoring rule to detect fingerprint aliasing and alert on config identity mismatches
Temporary weigher rule to prefer explicit route IDs over fingerprint lookup during promotion windows
action_items: ENG-241010: Fix route-predicate serializer to include stable namespace salt to eliminate same-cluster hash collisions - owner: Noah Patel - estimate: 8
ENG-241011: Add router-level collision detection that treats fingerprint collisions as fatal during promotions and falls back to full route comparison - owner: Maya Singh - estimate: 5
ENG-241012: Remove pin invariant from automated rollback path and replace with a reconciler that can safely unpin when promotion confidence passes safety gates - owner: Ava Martinez - estimate: 3
ENG-241013: Add end-to-end canary dry-run that validates route identity at all layers (translator, fanout, proxy) before enabling traffic - owner: Priya Rao - estimate: 5
ENG-241014: Post-deploy runbook update and on-call playbook for mixed-serve scenarios, include explicit steps for pin reconciliation - owner: Ops Team - estimate: 2
ENG-241015: Create a dashboard widget showing live route fingerprints and recent collisions across regions - owner: DataInfra - estimate: 3
postmortem_notes: Trade-off: Fingerprint indexing was chosen for speed; we under-budgeted for collision resistance in cross-version promotions.
Decision: Short-term fallback to explicit ID comparison during rollouts is acceptable until serializer fix is in place.
We determined customer impact was limited due to quick ops response, but reproducibility risk is high for high-churn rollout workflows.
Follow-ups will be tracked as discrete ENG tickets; no immediate customer communication required beyond internal account owners being notified.
risks_remaining: If serializer fix is delayed, similar collisions could happen for heterogeneous route predicates (header combos) and multi-region promotions.
Automated rollback remains a partial black box until pin reconciler behaviour is validated across test tenants.
